answer: For a decentralized cryptoeconomic security system to maintain anti-Sybil equilibrium, marginal attack costs must exceed any potential extracted value, rendering a voyage of attempting to exploit the network economically unfeasible. By introducing quadratic staking erosion rules, a substantial umber of capital expenditures is incurred with each additional attacker, scaling the marginal cost super-linearly, effectively creating a mirror effect where the cost of an attack far exceeds the value of the extracted resources, thus guaranteeing the security of the network.
